contents.p: The plain style of this coffin is typical of outer and middle coffins used in multi-piece ensembles between dynasty 22 and Dynasty 25. The vignettes on the chest, which shows the deceased in adoration before the baboon-formed god Thoth is unusual. We can only find one parallel, which is the coffin of Tatjenef at the National Museum of Scotland (A 1907.591).
Both coffins are unprovenienced, but based om the style of the interior coffin of Iwefaa, they likeley originated from the site of Akhmim in Upper Egypt.

The coffin PAHMA 6-19912 has two lines of inscription running vertically down the lid of the coffin from below the collar to the toes. These read in a retrograde fashion, with the first column on the viewer's left and the second on the viewer's right. The inscription is derived from a combination of Book of the Dead spells 51 and 52.

text.desc: Central columns on lid, reading retrograde and containing Book of the dead spell 51/52.

frag.al: Dd [mD.w] in wsir mn b(w).t=i sp-sn n wnm=i n xd.n=i Hr=f b(w).t=i pw Hs
frag.tr: Saying by the Osiris so-and-so: My Abomination! My Abomination! I shall not eat (it). I have not stepped on it. My abomination is feces.

frag.al: n wnm=i sw Htp-kA xr wsir mn i h<nw>.t nh.t {Iw=f-aA} HA.t-Hr{=i} t[…]
frag.tr: I shall not eat it, namely, excrement. The Osiris so-and-so shall not fall. Oh, Mistress of the Sycamore, {Iwefaa}, Hathor.

footnotes.fn: Johnston, Kea Marie, ‘Unseen Hands: Coffin Production at Akhmim, Dynasties 21-30’ (UC Berkeley, 2022) <https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3xp41156> [accessed 25 November 2022] pp 303, 304.
The scribe on this coffin does not differentiate between Gardiner A1 and Gardiner A2
Here, the glyph Gardiner D5 should have perhaps been used be instead of Gardiner U1.

The phrase Iw=f-aA is here taken to be the name of the deceased, inserted into the middle of the spell. The spelling with the bookroll determinative is odd, but is paralleled by the spelling of the name of the name of the deceased in the offering formula on the sides of the proposed inner coffin of this individual, PAHMA 6-19928

The spell after the word nh.t is a bit garbled. The last two signs seem to be determinatives for bread, but they are partially worn away, and the most that can be said about them is that they are probably long, flat signs.
